title: Pager cache configuration and shrink forwarding

scope.rationale: sqlite3PagerSetCachesize, sqlite3PagerSetSpillsize, and sqlite3PagerShrink are the Pager ownership boundary over PCache cache limits, spill update/query semantics, and group-wide release of unpinned clean pages.
excluded_responsibilities: PCache limit conversion and eviction internals

external_source_responsibilities: Owning B-tree or connection selects the Pager and holds required synchronization
dependencies.caller_closure: All three complete Pager forwarding bodies are assigned. Production release-memory dispatch calls shrinkCache on main and attached Pager owners; cache/spill methods preserve the PCache signed configuration boundary.

inputs: Live Pager and signed cache/spill configuration, or a shrink request
outputs: Updated PCache configuration, effective spill size, or count of released pages
contracts.ownership: Pager and PCache are borrowed connection owners. Shrink releases only PCache-owned unpinned clean pages.
contracts.state_and_results: Cache size always replaces configuration. Spill zero queries without mutation; nonzero replaces it and returns at least effective cache size. Shrink preserves pinned/dirty pages and Pager transaction state.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: PCache owns group synchronization. No callbacks or direct Pager I/O.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: The forwarding calls are infallible. Cache pressure may retain pages that are pinned or dirty; later operations continue on the same Pager.

representation_differences: The Pager methods expose the number of pages released by shrink even though the C wrapper discards the PCache result; callers may discard it to preserve the source API.
Signed KiB/page conversion remains in the existing native PCache owner rather than being duplicated in Pager.

oracle.protocol: Set positive and negative cache sizes, update and zero-query spill size, populate clean/unpinned plus retained pages, and shrink through the Pager methods; retain the 787-observation PCache differential and connection release-memory differential.
oracle.normalization: Configuration, counts, and state are exact; page addresses are identity-only.

assurance.oom: No Pager-wrapper allocation; PCache allocation and pressure paths have bounded deterministic coverage.
assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No direct I/O; PCache group locking and concurrent recycle are differentially and stress tested.
assurance.malformed_input: Signed cache/spill values preserve the existing bounded PCache conversion and zero-query rules.
assurance.continuation: Pinned/dirty pages survive shrink and later release/cleanup remains valid.
assurance.performance: Cache/spill forwarding is constant-time; shrink is bounded by purgeable group pages.

integration.native_call_path: Production Pager owns the PCache and sqlite3_db_release_memory invokes Pager.shrinkCache for main and attached databases; atomic-unit trace promotion awaits a scoped durable receipt.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Direct connection shrink bypass is retired in favor of the Pager source boundary.

independent_review.notes: Requires public PRAGMA cache/spill dispatch closure and independent review.

known_blockers: Capture a scoped Pager/PCache durable receipt before internal-trace promotion.
Route all public cache_size/cache_spill PRAGMA updates through the Pager owner.

src/core/pager.zig cache ownership, src/core/page_cache.zig signed configuration/group shrink, and connection release-memory callers were reviewed
callers: Connection-wide sqlite3_db_release_memory on main and attached databases
assertions_branches_cleanup: The only active source behavior block is the spill return and is assigned
Cache and shrink wrappers are straight forwarding bodies
PCache owns all release and retained-page cleanup
upstream_tests: Upstream cache-size, cache-spill, shrink, release-memory, PCache, OOM, and mutex tests cover this boundary
